Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Gajendra Singh

On The 10th Of March, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 1042 of 2023
 Smt. Pooja And Others
 Versus
 Assemsingh Dandel And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Himanshu Paliwal, learned counsel for the appellant
 Shri Bhashkar Agrawal, learned counsel for the responden
 Order

This miscellaneous appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 30.06.2022 in MACC No.3242/2018 by 20th Addl. MACT, Indore for enhancement of Rs.8 lakhs as compensation.
The liability is not in dispute.

2. The brief facts are that a total compensation of Rs.20,68,932/-
was awarded for the death of Ashish Shukla, aged 26 years working as sales representative in PRK Commodities Ltd. in a motor accident on 11.08.2018 at Tejaji Nagar, Khandwa Road, Indore.
3. Tribunal calculated a total compensation of Rs.19,03,932/- under the head of loss of dependency assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/- per month, adding 40% towards future NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6559 2 MA-1042-2023 prospects, deducting 1/3rd for personal expenses and applying the multiplier of 17.
4.

This appeal is preferred on the ground that the income has been assessed on the lower side without taking into consideration the testimony of Mahendra (PW/2), salary certificate Ex.P/12,
bank passbook Ex.P/13 & 14 and ledger statement of PRK Commodities Pvt. Ltd, 87/5, Himmat Nagar Road, Palda, Indore (Ex.P/21).
5. Counsel for the respondent opposed the enhancement.
6. Perused the record and the testimony of Supervisor Mahenra (PW/2), Ex.P/12, P/13, P/14 and P/21.
The documentary evidence cannot be ignored.

In this case the Tribunal ought to have assessed Smt. Pooja vs Assemsingh Dandel on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15372613/
1 the income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- per month instead of Rs.10,000/- and adding 40%
towards future prospects the income ought to have been calculated as Rs.21,000/- per month.
The rest of the amount was properly awarded.

Accordingly, the compensation is recalculated as under:
Rs.28,56,000/-
Loss of dependency (i.e. Rs.15,000+6000 (40% FP) =21,000x12=2,52,000-1/3 PE=1,68,000x17(M)

Loss of Rs.1,32,000/-
consortium Loss of estate Rs.16,500/- Funeral Rs.16,500/-
 expenses

Total Rs.30,21,000/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6559 3 MA-1042-2023 7.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.30,21,000/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.20,68,932/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.9,52,068/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.9,52,068/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
9. The appellant has valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.8 lakhs and paid the Court fee accordingly.

However, for the remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellants within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
10. In the result, the appeal is allowed to the extent indicated herein above.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE hk/
